ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the diamond $ABCD$, $AB=BD=5$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, \\
$\therefore$ AB=AD, and AC bisects $\angle$BAD, \\
Since AB=BD=5, \\
$\therefore$ AB=AD=BD, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ABD is an equilateral triangle, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BAD$=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BAC$=\boxed{30^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a rhombus/diamond-shaped quadrilateral ABCD, with A on the left, C on the right, D on top, and B on the bottom; diagonal AC is drawn horizontally, diagonal DB is drawn vertically, and they intersect inside at O. What is required is the angle between BA and AC at point A, namely ∠BAC. Reasoning: The problem gives that ABCD is a diamond, namely a rhombus, so the four sides are equal. Given AB=5, therefore AD=5. Also given BD=5. Thus in triangle ABD, AB=AD=BD=5, it is an equilateral triangle, so ∠DAB=60°. In a rhombus, diagonal AC bisects angle A, therefore ∠BAC is half of ∠DAB, namely 60°/2=30°.

method.method_draft: First read the figure as a rhombus/diamond ABCD with A at the left, C at the right, D at the top, B at the bottom, and diagonal AC drawn through A and C; the requested angle BAC is the angle between side BA and diagonal AC at A. From the text, use that ABCD is a diamond and AB=BD=5. Since a diamond/rhombus has all sides equal, AD=AB=5, so in triangle ABD we have AB=AD=BD=5. Therefore triangle ABD is equilateral and angle DAB is 60 degrees. In a rhombus, diagonal AC bisects the angle at A, so angle BAC is half of angle DAB: 30 degrees.
